How the shape was derived

The client's site plan was digitized by colour: plot, building zone, patio, garden and paving, street-fitted to OSM. The yellow zone (13,500 m²) is far larger than any tabled floor plate, so the building is a slender curved bar along the zone's own spine — exactly the proportion the hand sketches show. Each floor is the bar cut at a length solved so the plate nets its tabled area; the tabled areas grow linearly, so the NW end face comes out as one straight raked plane on its own.

Ground and level 1 form a vertical podium set back 7 m under the rake; levels 2–3 are pushed onto the rake line and gain ~860 m² (declared in the schedule); every other level is exact to 0.0 m².

The datum

The Sail Tower's ground zero is not the street: it stands on the existing raised plaza — a multi-storey structure whose roof is the deck, here modelled +10 m over the new building's grade. The garden terraces step down from that deck to the new building's forecourt.

Fixed inputs

  • 5 basements at 2.80 m, 3,200 m² each
  • Ground and level 1 at 5.00 m
  • Levels 2–21 at m
  • Patio open from grade through the roof, constant in plan

The neighbour

The tower next door is the Sail Tower (מגדל המפרש), Building B of the Rabin Government Complex on Derech HaAtzma'ut, and the building the brief calls בניין הטיל. Amer–Curiel Architects, 1999–2002: 29 storeys, main roof at 95 m, sail tips at 113 m, antenna at 137 m. It is modelled on its surveyed OSM footprint at those published heights.

Surroundings

—

  • Buildings, streets and the shoreline: OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
  • Terrain: SRTM 30 m, sampled on a 50 m grid — enough for the Carmel slope, too coarse for individual port quays.
  • Heights are shown relative to grade at the site, which SRTM puts at m above sea level.

The compass

—

Read with care

  • The plot bearing is °, measured from the OSM centrelines of Derech HaAtzma'ut. Plan proportions still come from the sketches, not from a survey.
  • The plot's position is fixed relative to the Sail Tower as drawn on the client's site plan; OSM then fixes the Sail Tower on the globe.
  • Most context buildings have no height in OSM and are drawn at an assumed 4 storeys — indicative fabric, not survey.
  • Basements are shown as one plate enlarged about the tower centroid; in reality they would run asymmetrically under the plaza.
